discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
motivation: In 2013 the IceCube Neutrino Observatory at the South Pole reported the first unambiguous detection of a flux of high-energy neutrinos of extraterrestrial origin, at TeV-PeV energies. This opened a new window on the universe: neutrinos travel undeflected by magnetic fields and unabsorbed by matter, so they point back to the most violent cosmic accelerators. Subsequent observations identified the blazar TXS 0506+056 (2017) and the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068 (2022) as neutrino sources and imaged the Galactic plane in neutrinos (2023). Francis Halzen conceived the idea of instrumenting a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice and, over three decades, led the scientific and technical effort through AMANDA to IceCube, overcoming formidable challenges in deep-ice drilling, optical calibration and background rejection. The discovery is sharply defined, firmly established, and has founded the field of high-energy neutrino astronomy and multi-messenger astrophysics.
